text:
Victor: Hi folks, day 1 on WSL2 (Ubuntu). I followed the Linux onboarding but my home dotfiles assume macOS paths and `brew` commands. I installed Homebrew on WSL (linuxbrew) but asdf still chooses wrong python and node versions. Any tips to get parity with the team's devcontainer?

Sam: Welcome Victor! On WSL we prefer `asdf` + `asdf` plugins rather than distro packages. First, ensure you `asdf install` from the repo `.tool-versions` with `asdf install --no-checksums`. For Homebrew on Linux keep it under `~/.linuxbrew` and use `eval "$($(brew --prefix)/bin/brew shellenv)"` in your ~/.profile.

Victor: There is no .tool-versions in the repo. CI uses py3.9 + node16. Should I add one locally?

Mira: If theres no file, set `asdf local python 3.9.13` and `asdf local nodejs 16.20.0` in the project dir. Then `direnv allow`. We ask folks to open a quick PR adding `.tool-versions` to pin runtimes for the team.

Victor: Node plugin failed: `gpg: cannot open tty` when running the plugin import script. I tried `gpg --card-status` and it asks for a pinpad; I don't have a YubiKey.

Alex: For non-YubiKey machines you can import the public keyring without smartcard: `brew install gnupg` then `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` or run the plugin with `-s` to skip verification if necessary. Prefer installing gnupg and importing keys.

Victor: My SSH agent isn't forwarding into the VS Code remote WSL session so I can't push. Any standard setup?

Sam: In VS Code Remote for WSL enable "Remote.SSH: Agent" or forward your socket with `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(gpgconf --list-dirs agent-extra-socket)` if using gpg-agent. For the WSL case, use `socat` to forward the Windows SSH agent or use the built-in Adapter: `wsl --shutdown` then in Windows start `ssh-agent` and add keys. There's a handbook section with exact steps.

Victor: Where do folks store local DB creds? The repo has `.envrc.sample` but not `.envrc`. I'm wary of copying creds into files.

Mira: 1Password is canonical. Use the 1Password CLI in your `.envrc` like: `export DATABASE_URL=$(op item get "redwood/dev-db" --fields password)` then `direnv allow`. We avoid committing real env files.

Victor: Dotfiles contain mac-specific functions like `open` and `.macos` logic. Best way to keep my fork working on WSL without breaking mac users?

Alex: Add a small OS check in the dotfiles: `if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Linux" ]; then source dotfiles/linux.sh; fi` and keep mac code in `macos.sh`. Open a PR to add `linux.sh` with equivalents using `xdg-open` and linuxbrew paths. Mention WSL in the PR body.

Victor: Thanks! One last micro-ask: CI pins Cargo toolchain; should I use rustup on WSL too?

Sam: Yes, use rustup everywhere dev is done. `rustup toolchain install stable-2023-10-01` (or whatever in `rust-toolchain.toml`) then `rustup default` that. Keeps parity with CI.

infra-bot: Heads up: onboarding doc updated with WSL notes for Homebrew/linuxbrew, asdf plugin GPG steps, and SSH forwarding tips. https://go.redwood/handbook/onboarding/setup

Victor: Great, that unblocks me. I'll add local `.tool-versions` and open the dotfiles PR. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
